GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The skill answers "what were we doing in this project?" by reading OpenCode's own session storage, so it observes the OpenCode tooling itself rather than guiding the work protocol. README's managed-skills section defines exactly this split: vv-* skills guide work protocol and craft companions, vvoc-* skills operate and observe the vvoc/OpenCode tooling. The closest existing sibling is vvoc-usage-analytics, which also performs read-only analysis over opencode.db; adopting the vvoc- prefix and the full domain phrase (project + session + history) keeps the name precise and consistent with that precedent. The extractor script is frozen byte-identically at the 2026-11-25 direct fix because that version was verified against a live pure-V2 database, a V1+V2 mixed fixture, and a V1-only fixture (25 checks), and re-opening extraction logic inside a bundling change would mix two risk profiles for no benefit. SKILL.md, in contrast, is deliberately restructured rather than transferred: the canonical six-block grammar gate applies to every shipped template, so a plain-markdown port would fail the suite the change itself must satisfy. The scripts/ capability was chosen over reusing references/ because the executable file is semantically not agent-readable documentation, the skill's run command should keep the conventional scripts/ path, and the references/ contract (on-demand material the agent opens) should not be stretched to carry executables; the cost is a small parallel delivery path that mirrors the proven references/ implementation. That mirroring is deliberately literal: scripts carry no per-file ownership marker, so delivery uses pure template content comparison gated only by the parent SKILL.md skip state — the same semantics references already have, with no script-level frontmatter guard (a .py file has no YAML frontmatter, so such a guard would permanently skip every shipped script). The staleness inspection is extended to scripts for the same reason: a silently stale installed script is precisely the pre-fix failure mode this bundle exists to retire. Legacy standalone copies are left for manual removal because vvoc must never silently remove user-owned files outside its managed directories, and the rename to vvoc-project-session-history already avoids a path collision, so nothing forces an automatic migration.

Alternatives.Alternative: Name the skill vv-project-session-history, framing session-start context recovery as work protocol that complements vv-handoff (handoff writes notes at session end, this reads the past). Rejected: the README family split classifies by function for the user, and reading OpenCode's own database is tooling observation, not work-protocol guidance.

Name it vvoc-session-recap or vvoc-project-history. Rejected: "recap" drops the project scoping that the extractor defaults to, and "project history" reads wider than session history and can be confused with Git history.

Ship the script inside references/ and have SKILL.md run python3 against references/project_history.py. Rejected: zero-machinery but semantically wrong — references are on-demand documentation opened by the agent, and the executable would be the only non-document reference in the bundle.
Inline the extractor into SKILL.md. Rejected: roughly 500 lines of Python inside the instruction file, unmaintainable and incompatible with the self-sufficient-core-plus-references skill structure.

Have vvoc detect and remove or migrate the legacy standalone copy during install/sync. Rejected: violates the never-clobber-user-owned-config invariant for a benefit (avoiding interim duplicate skill descriptions) that a one-line manual instruction covers.

Rewrite project_history.py in TypeScript for the Bun runtime. Rejected: the Python script is verified as-is, Python 3 is present on both machines, and a rewrite would re-open the fixed extraction logic that this change explicitly freezes.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Whether later skills may ship additional executable or binary assets, and whether scripts/ delivery grows a general extra-files mechanism, is deferred until a second consumer exists; this change ships the flat scripts/ sibling of references/ only.

Whether the grammar/reference gates gain a dedicated scripts/ lint (for example, a Python syntax check in CI) is deferred; the current gate set asserts delivery and content markers, not script linting.
Whether the standalone skill's empty references/ and assets/ directories ever gain content is deferred; nothing ships for them now.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user on a host whose database is pure V2 (no session/message/part tables) asks for a project recap: the installed skill runs, lists sessions from session_v2, reads session_message, excludes reasoning and tool parts, and returns recent sessions instead of failing with "database has no session table".

A host with a mixed V1+V2 database (legacy tables frozen around 2026-10-02) asks the same: the UNION session list returns both eras exactly once per session, dual-store messages deduplicate, and pre-V2 sessions keep their legacy message text.

vvoc sync runs on a machine where a previous bundled version installed the script and the user later edited the installed copy: sync sees differing content and updates it back to the template, matching the references/ contract.

vvoc sync runs on a machine where the parent SKILL.md path holds a user-owned file without YAML frontmatter and the skill is skipped: neither the skill nor its script path is written, so a user file at the script path under that skipped parent survives untouched. A user-created file at the script path under a non-skipped, vvoc-managed parent is refreshed to the template, exactly as references behave.

A machine still carrying the standalone ~/.config/opencode/skills/project-session-history runs vvoc sync after upgrading: the bundled vvoc-project-session-history installs, the legacy copy stays untouched, and the user removes it manually after confirming the bundled skill works.
